Subject: SIG intake — SSO/SCIM/RBAC details needed for onboarding

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for agreeing to help close out Acme Health's SIG intake. The assessor has a few targeted asks around access controls for the pilot deployment:

- Confirm supported SSO protocols (SAML/OIDC) and whether IdP-initiated vs SP-initiated is supported.
- SCIM: full list of attributes you accept for provisioning, and whether we support delta vs full sync.
- RBAC: sample role matrix for onboarding (roles, permissions, default least-privilege mapping).
- MFA: which authentication factors are enforced at the application level vs delegated to the IdP.
- Evidence: screenshots, SCIM schema export, RBAC CSV, and a short narrative describing least-privilege defaults.

Target: can you provide a consolidated packet by next Wednesday (2025-09-24)? If useful, I can schedule a quick call to walk the assessor through any items.

Appreciate it — Jordan
Jordan Miller
Security Review Lead, Acme Health
jmiller@acmehealth.com

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: SIG intake — SSO/SCIM/RBAC details needed for onboarding

Jordan — thanks for the clear list. We've started collecting artifacts and I attached an initial response workbook that maps the SIG questions to our evidence. Highlights below; see attachment for the full matrix.

Attachments: sig-responses-v0.1.xlsx (response matrix with pointers to screenshots and exported schemas)

Quick answers / summary:
- SSO: We support SAML 2.0 and OIDC. Both IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows are supported; for SAML we include SP metadata for the customer and can accept IdP metadata uploads.
- SCIM: SCIM 2.0 compliant. We support both bulk and incremental (PATCH) provisioning; our supported attribute set is in the SCIM tab of the workbook.
- RBAC: Default roles (Viewer, Editor, Admin) are documented in the Roles tab with permission scopes. We recommend least-privilege by default — new users are provisioned as Viewer unless the customer requests elevate-on-first-login.
- MFA: We delegate primary MFA enforcement to the customer's IdP (recommended). For hosted customers who opt for Redwood-managed auth, we enforce TOTP + recovery flow.

Open items for you:
1) Which specific SCIM attributes does Acme use for department/team mapping? If they use a custom attribute, we can include mapping guidance.
2) For the pilot, do you want us to include a screenshot of the SAML configuration page and the assertion example? (we can include sanitized screenshots).

If that's all good, Dev will attach the RBAC export and the SCIM mapping file in a follow-up.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Date: 2025-09-21T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG intake — SCIM & RBAC artifacts

Aisha / team — attaching the exports requested. I included a SCIM attribute mapping CSV and a printable RBAC matrix PDF. Notes below.

Attachments: scim-role-map.csv, rbac-matrix.pdf

Notes:
- SCIM: scim-role-map.csv contains the attribute names we accept (userName, externalId, displayName, emails, groups) and our recommended mapping for Acme's department/team attributes (we support custom attribute mapping via the admin console or API). We support PATCH for incremental provisioning; our SCIM endpoint returns 200 with standard error codes.
- RBAC: rbac-matrix.pdf contains the three-tier role set and the specific API/UI permissions tied to each role. A few clarifications:
  * Admin role includes user management + billing visibility.
  * Editor can create and manage inference routes and prompts but cannot modify billing settings.
  * Viewer is read-only for dashboards and logs.
- SAML assertion: we include nameID (transient/persistent), groups claim (optional), and an attributes block that can include department/team if the IdP sends it. If Acme wants to use groups for coarse-grained authorization we recommend sending group membership in the assertion.
- MFA: as Aisha said, we strongly recommend enforcing MFA at the IdP. For customers that rely on Redwood-managed auth, MFA (TOTP) is enforced at first login and every 90 days by default.

If someone from Acme wants a short technical walkthrough of the SCIM webhook behavior and error codes, I can join the call.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: scim-role-map.csv (text/csv)]
